name: P-MMEval
l2: 并行多语言多任务评测
intro: P-MMEval 是通义实验室构建的平行多语言多任务基准。最终论文直接选择 XNLI、MHellaSwag、FLORES-200 三个基础组成部分和 HumanEval-XL、MGSM、MLogiQA、MMMLU、MIFEval 五个专项组成部分，按各数据集规则抽样后，用 gpt-4o-2024-05-13 补齐缺失语言并由专业翻译团队穷尽复核，最终在十种语言上比较任务表现与跨语言迁移一致性。
build_method: 三项基础与五项专项数据选择, 数据集专用抽样, GPT-4o补译, 专业翻译穷尽复核与本地化
language: 英文, 中文, 阿拉伯文, 西班牙文, 日文, 韩文, 泰文, 法文, 葡萄牙文, 越南文
task_type: 多语言理解与生成, 数学与逻辑推理, 代码生成, 指令遵循
eval_feature: 十语言平行样本, 英文/母语/英文少样本提示, 任务指标与CACR跨语言一致性
scale: 8个组成部分、7类任务、10种语言；21,580条自然语言题面，计入HumanEval-XL的12种编程语言后为30,380个表列单元
task_type_en: Multilingual understanding and generation, Math and logical reasoning, Code generation, Instruction following
build_method_en: Three Fundamental and Five Specialized Dataset Selection, Dataset-specific Sampling, GPT-4o Translation Completion, Exhaustive Professional Review and Localization
eval_feature_en: Parallel Samples in Ten Languages, English/Native/English Few-shot Prompts, Task Metrics and CACR Transfer Consistency
intro_en: P-MMEval is a parallel multilingual multitask benchmark from Tongyi Lab. The final paper directly selects three fundamental components—XNLI, MHellaSwag, and FLORES-200—and five specialized components—HumanEval-XL, MGSM, MLogiQA, MMMLU, and MIFEval. It applies dataset-specific sampling, completes missing languages with gpt-4o-2024-05-13, performs exhaustive professional translation review, and compares task performance and transfer consistency across ten languages.
language_en: English, Chinese, Arabic, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Thai, French, Portuguese, Vietnamese
scale_en: 8 components, 7 tasks, and 10 languages; 21,580 natural-language items or 30,380 table units after HumanEval-XL's 12-program execution dimension

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; source_stage=site-a12c-openskill-pmmeval. P-MMEval was reconstructed from the fixed arXiv:2411.09116v2 PDF, SHA-256 00f32884b4d5f08b5ecd601d7be71099f8b2559cc2f927c5d8b3adf0d1bf3a7d; the final EMNLP 2025 ACL Anthology paper 2025.emnlp-main.242, PDF SHA-256 17f87baa7ede625651e2d5bd6687a1193922269f7ca3ea846f57b79ddac8fdd4; and the official Qwen/P-MMEval dataset revision 47bb647f35fdd6f5374826b3f5d4f84eb5b5afce. The fixed dataset card has SHA-256 36c20135369fe3df20e86ef7afbcec202021c1cdb28e27b36bfbbb621eb04390. The final paper's Sections 3.1–3.4 do not describe an eleven-dataset candidate pool, three model-size screening pairs, a paired-sample t-test, or a p<0.01 admission gate. Those claims were removed rather than preserved as construction steps. The paper directly selects three fundamental components—XNLI and MHellaSwag for understanding plus FLORES-200 for generation—and five capability-specialized components: HumanEval-XL for code generation, MGSM for mathematical reasoning, MLogiQA for logical reasoning, MMMLU for knowledge, and MIFEval for instruction following. Section 3.1 fixes English, Chinese, Arabic, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Thai, French, Portuguese, and Vietnamese and explicitly says they span seven language families. The pinned Hugging Face card instead says eight language families while listing the same ten languages; the diagram follows the paper and records the card discrepancy as a dashed boundary. Appendix A supplies dataset-specific sampling rather than a global statistical screen. FLORES-200 retains its complete 1,012-example test set without additional translation. HumanEval-XL's 80 and MGSM's 250 examples per language are translated in full. XNLI, MHellaSwag, and MLogiQA select the first N source examples, yielding intended per-language counts of 120, 120, and 80. MMMLU uses six models as a difficulty proxy, forms a 6,335-item all-easy pool and a 663-item all-hard pool, applies MMLU-Redux corrections and subject filtering, then samples 200 easy plus 200 hard. For MIFEval, Appendix A says to select ten examples per task type, producing 110 examples, then remove 14 during translation verification to leave 96; it does not enumerate those sampling groups there. Section 3.4 names gpt-4o-2024-05-13 for missing-language translation. A professional translation team exhaustively reviews the machine output, corrects errors, localizes vocabulary, reconciles terminology, and removes instances that do not translate well. Table 2's largest modification rate is 82.50% for Japanese MHellaSwag; this supports the human-review stage and warns against treating raw machine translation as final data. Table 1 defines eight components over seven tasks with the intended per-language counts: FLORES 1,012; XNLI 120; MHellaSwag 120; HumanEval-XL 80 across 12 programming languages; MGSM 250; MLogiQA 80; MMMLU 400; and MIFEval 96. Summing one natural-language task record before the HumanEval programming-language multiplier gives 21,580 items across ten languages. Applying Table 1's explicit HumanEval-XL ×12 programming-language dimension gives 30,380 table units; therefore the old unqualified phrase '21,580 language-specific instances' was replaced with this two-level count. Section 3.5 adapts prompts from OpenCompass and the LM Evaluation Harness, adds fixed answer-format constraints to improve extraction, translates instructions for Native prompts, and uses OpenAI simple-evals for MMMLU. Section 4.2 compares EN, Native, and EN-Few-Shot. Few-shot demonstrations come primarily from validation data and missing-language demonstrations are translated with GPT-4o. MGSM uses chain-of-thought, while other tasks use direct answers; models below 7B are evaluated with direct answers because chain-of-thought outputs caused extraction failures. The main metrics are Accuracy for classification, reasoning, knowledge, and instruction-following components; BLEU for FLORES-200; and Pass@1 for HumanEval-XL. HumanEval results in the main comparison average Python, JavaScript, and Java. COMET is reported in an appendix but is not the primary FLORES metric. Formula 1 defines CACR from English to a target language as jointly correct parallel items divided by English-correct items, so CACR requires instance alignment rather than independent language aggregates. The fixed release has material, documented boundaries. Its card declares Apache-2.0 and its file tree is broader or smaller than several Table 1 cells. FLORES contains 9 files and 9,108 rows, representing nine English-to-target files rather than a ten-file 10,120-row matrix. Table 1 states MHellaSwag 120 × 10, but the fixed release has 1,181 rows: ar 116, en 120, es 119, fr 116, ja 120, ko 120, pt 116, th 120, vi 120, and zh 114. Consequently, fixed-release cross-language comparisons must use common aligned IDs and cannot assume every language contains all 120 intended items. The raw HumanEval-XL tree contains 26 natural-language files under each of 12 programming-language directories, not only the ten P-MMEval languages; consumers must explicitly select the paper's ten-language scope. At audit time the Hugging Face datasets server materialized 19,749 non-HumanEval rows and reported the HumanEval-XL config as failed, so its loader summary is not evidence for the paper's full 30,380-unit matrix. The pinned card points users to OpenCompass commands but does not itself publish a complete executable reproduction of all three paper settings. The paper does not disclose general decoding parameters, random seeds, stop sequences, or a per-task few-shot k, so the diagram marks these as inference boundaries rather than inventing values. No dedicated P-MMEval leaderboard or formal submission service is claimed. No formal Draw.io, SVG, PNG, architecture sidecar, catalog, or manifest was changed in this source-stage pass. Formal publication evidence [site-a12c-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2285×1001 (English) and 2285×1001 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2283×999 and 2283×999. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
